title: Best Marathon Running Shoes
excerpt: Marathon racing shoes, training shoes and comfort picks, from the Nike Alphafly 3 to the Saucony Endorphin Speed 5, with list prices.
body:
Best Marathon Running Shoes

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

A marathon shoe has to stay comfortable for hours, not just feel fast at the start. This guide covers racing shoes, training shoes for the build-up and cushioned picks for runners who prioritise comfort. It's based on manufacturer specs and published reviews. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update.

Racing shoes

  • Nike Alphafly 3 ($295): a carbon-plated road racer.
  • Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 4 ($250): a versatile racer with a 39 mm heel stack and a 6 mm drop.
  • Hoka Cielo X1 3.0 ($275): released in January 2026. Reviewers describe it as fast but aggressive.
  • ASICS Metaspeed Sky Tokyo ($270): for runners who speed up by lengthening their stride.
  • ASICS Metaspeed Edge Tokyo ($270): for runners who speed up by increasing cadence.

Training shoes for the build-up

  • Saucony Endorphin Speed 5 ($175): a nylon-plated trainer for marathon-pace runs and workouts.
  • ASICS Superblast 3 ($210): a light, high-stack trainer that many runners also race in.
  • ASICS Megablast ($225): a high-cushion super trainer for long runs.

Comfort-first picks

  • Nike Vomero Plus ($180): maximum cushion for long runs, and for race day if comfort is your priority.
  • Brooks Glycerin 23 ($180): soft, neutral cushioning.
  • Adidas Adizero EVO SL ($150): a light, unplated shoe that works for both training and racing.

Trail marathons

The Hoka Tecton X 3 lists at $275 and is a plated trail racing shoe for runnable trail marathons and ultras.

How to choose

  • Chasing a time: a plated racer, such as the Nike Alphafly 3, Adidas Adios Pro 4, Hoka Cielo X1 3.0 or ASICS Metaspeed. Choose the ASICS Sky or Edge to match how you run.
  • Finishing comfortably: a cushioned trainer you trust, such as the Nike Vomero Plus or Brooks Glycerin 23.
  • Whatever you race in: do your longest runs in it first. Plated shoes feel different late in a long run, and race day isn't the time to find out how.

Research and race results suggest plated "super shoes" make many runners more economical, but the benefit varies from runner to runner.
